claims.text: High configurational entropy governs an HEA's ability to develop and retain a protective oxide layer.
High configurational entropy causes sluggish diffusion in HEAs.
Sluggish diffusion promotes selective oxidation of reactive elements such as Cr or Al.
Selective oxidation of Cr or Al forms a dense, adherent protective oxide scale.
Arc melting followed by homogenization ensures a well-mixed microstructure with evenly distributed reactive elements.
Oxidation at 1100°C for 24 to 100 hours in air is the proposed test condition.
A binary or ternary alloy with comparable reactive-element content but lower configurational entropy is the proposed control.
The HEA will form a selectively enriched Cr2O3 or Al2O3 scale.
The selectively enriched oxide scale will be dense, adherent, and slow-growing.
Reduced metal-cation mobility in the high-entropy microstructure mediates formation of the protective scale.
The sluggish-diffusion effect retards transport of both metal ions and oxygen.
Retarded transport favors formation of protective oxide islands that coalesce into a continuous barrier.
The continuous oxide barrier limits further oxidation and preserves the alloy core.
Relative to the conventional-alloy control, the HEA will form a thicker oxide layer.
Relative to the control, the HEA oxide layer will be more uniform and adherent.
Relative to the control, the HEA will exhibit a lower oxidation rate and lower weight gain.
The hypothesis primarily applies above 900°C, where diffusion mechanisms are activated.
The hypothesis may not apply at very low temperatures, very high oxygen pressures, or in non-oxidizing environments.
Sluggish diffusion in HEAs is well supported in the literature.
Similar or higher oxidation rates, poor scale integrity, or less-selective oxidation in the HEA than in the control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The mediator and mechanism describe a slow-growing barrier that limits further oxidation, while the predicted outcome treats a thicker scale as evidence of superior protection and the falsification rule also requires it to be thicker. Greater thickness is not inherently consistent with slower scale growth or lower oxidation, so the directional prediction is internally misaligned.
